questions.q: What is the foundation of any research project, according to Data Carpentry?
questions.explain: Badly organised data causes errors in every later step.
questions.evidence: Good data organization is the foundation of any research project.

questions.q: What is a drawback of doing data cleaning or analysis in a spreadsheet?
options: It is not easy to show or replicate what you did
questions.explain: Spreadsheets are good for data entry; scripted tools keep a record of each step.
questions.evidence: Spreadsheets are good for data entry, but when doing data cleaning or analysis, it's not easy to show or replicate what you did.

questions.q: What should you always do before changing data?
options: Make a copy — never modify your raw data
questions.explain: Keeping raw data untouched means you can always start again.
questions.evidence: Never modify your raw data. Always make a copy before making any changes.

questions.q: Why should you avoid spreading one dataset across multiple tabs?
options: The computer can't see the connections in the data
Each tab needs its own password
questions.explain: Keep one table per dataset; use a separate tab only to record cleaning notes.
questions.evidence: When you create extra tabs, you fail to allow the computer to see connections in the data that are there

questions.q: What is a good practice to avoid ambiguity in dates?
options: Always use the local date format
Split dates into separate YEAR, MONTH and DAY columns
questions.explain: Regional formats and software differences make single date cells risky.
questions.evidence: a good practice is to divide dates into components in different columns - YEAR, MONTH, and DAY.

questions.q: How can you prevent invalid data being entered by accident?
questions.explain: Validation rules restrict cells to allowed values or ranges.
questions.evidence: Use data validation to prevent accidentally entering invalid data.

questions.q: Why export spreadsheet data to a universal format such as CSV?
options: Common spreadsheet formats are often not read correctly by analysis software
questions.explain: Proprietary formats may also become hard to open in the future.
questions.evidence: Data stored in common spreadsheet formats will often not be read correctly into data analysis software, introducing errors into your data.

questions.q: Why are closed questions often better in forms?
options: They are easier to answer than open questions
questions.explain: Users of government services are often afraid of being caught out by open questions.
questions.evidence: Closed questions are easier to answer than open questions

questions.q: What do 'branching' questions do in a form?
options: Let users skip the whole form
Mean people only answer questions relevant to them
questions.explain: Shorter, relevant journeys reduce errors and abandoned forms.
questions.evidence: Use ‘branching’ questions so people only have to answer questions that are relevant to them.

questions.q: What is the first thing to do when planning to collect personal information?
options: Remove any questions you do not need to ask
Add a consent checkbox to every page
Collect everything in case it is useful
Ask for an ID number first
questions.explain: Collect only what you need — and check with your data protection adviser.
questions.evidence: The first thing to do is remove any questions that you do not need to ask

questions.q: What is the most common mistake people make with spreadsheets?
options: Treating them like lab notebooks, relying on notes, layout and context
questions.explain: Computers can't read margin notes or layout — only well-structured data.
questions.evidence: The most common mistake made is treating spreadsheet programs like lab notebooks

questions.q: What is the rule of thumb for setting up a datasheet?
options: One table per tab, with colours for categories
Notes in the margin and totals at the bottom
Merged cells for headings and comments for units
Each variable in its own column, each observation in its own row, one value per cell
questions.explain: These are the tidy data principles.
questions.evidence: should have its own column, each observation should have its own row, and each cell should contain only a single value

questions.q: When should you set up well-formatted tables?
options: From the outset, before entering any data
questions.explain: Fixing structure later is much more work than getting it right first.
questions.evidence: it's extremely important to set up well-formatted tables from the outset

questions.q: Where should metadata about your data be kept?
options: In the first rows of the data file
Separately, not inside the data file
questions.explain: Metadata in the data file can disrupt how programs read it.
questions.evidence: However, metadata should not be contained in the data file itself.

questions.q: Why is recording metadata essential?
options: You are unlikely to remember details, like a question's exact wording, later
Spreadsheets refuse to open without it
questions.explain: Metadata documents what each column means and how it was collected.
questions.evidence: the chances that you will still remember the exact wording of the question you asked

questions.q: What does a blank cell tell the computer?
options: That the value repeats the one above
That the cell is a header
That the value is unknown or missing (null)
questions.explain: Blanks and zeros mean different things to analysis software.
questions.evidence: A blank cell means that it wasn't measured and the computer will interpret it as an unknown value (otherwise known as a null value).

questions.q: Why must zeros be recorded as zeros rather than left blank?
options: A blank is read as missing data, which means something different
questions.explain: Use a clear, consistent indicator for truly missing values.
questions.evidence: it's very important to record zeros as zeros and truly missing data as nulls

questions.q: Why should you avoid merged cells?
options: They make data unreadable by statistics software
questions.explain: Analysis tools expect one value per cell in a regular grid.
questions.evidence: Merged cells will make your data unreadable by statistics software.

questions.q: What is a good alternative to spaces in column names?
questions.explain: Spaces and special characters cause trouble in many programs.
questions.evidence: Underscores ( _ ) are a good alternative to spaces.

questions.q: When is it fine to add a new tab to your spreadsheet?
options: To store each year's data separately
To hold each site's data separately
To keep a second copy of the table
To record the cleaning or changes you made to the data
questions.explain: Splitting the data itself across tabs hides connections from the computer.
questions.evidence: but do use a new tab to record data cleaning or manipulations

questions.q: Why are spreadsheet date functions risky when sharing data?
options: They only work in leap years
They convert dates to text automatically
They are only guaranteed to work within the same family of software
They are disabled in CSV files
questions.explain: Storing year, month and day in separate columns avoids the problem.
questions.evidence: functions are guaranteed to be compatible only within the same family of software products

questions.q: Which validation rule fits a column recording age in years?
options: Numeric, greater than 0 and unlikely to exceed 120
questions.explain: Validation stops impossible values at the moment of entry.
questions.evidence: For example a column recording age in years should be numeric, greater than 0 and is unlikely to be greater than 120.

questions.q: A column only accepts entries from a list. What happens if you type a value that isn't on it?
options: It is added to the list
questions.explain: A drop-down list also shows the allowed values.
questions.evidence: If you type a value which is not on the list, you will get an error message.

questions.q: When you set up data validation, what should you also create?
options: An informative error alert and input message
questions.explain: Good messages tell the person entering data what is expected.
questions.evidence: Be sure to create an informative error alert and input message.

questions.q: Whom should you consult to check that collecting personal information is proportionate?
options: Your data protection expert or legal adviser
questions.explain: They can confirm your plans are proportionate in the circumstances.
questions.evidence: Talk to your data protection expert or legal adviser to make sure what you

questions.q: Your service stores information on users' devices using cookies. What must you do?
options: Follow the guidance about using cookies
questions.explain: Cookies and similar technologies have their own rules.
questions.evidence: you must follow the guidance about using cookies

questions.q: You only need to know whether someone receives a benefit. What should you avoid storing?
options: The raw personal information, such as a scan of their benefit letter
The fact that they are eligible
questions.explain: Keep only what you need, for no longer than you need it.
questions.evidence: And avoid storing the raw personal information they supplied (for example, a scan of the benefit letter that proved their eligibility).

questions.q: Must you always store the personal information you collect?
options: Yes, for at least ten years
No — sometimes you don't need to store it at all
questions.explain: Never keep personal data longer than necessary.
questions.evidence: You do not always need to store personal information at all.

questions.q: In OpenRefine, what does clustering mean?
options: Finding groups of different values that may represent the same thing
questions.explain: It is ideal for merging spelling variants into one value.
questions.evidence: finding groups of different values that might be alternative representations of the same thing

questions.q: Which data problems is clustering especially good at fixing?
questions.explain: Clusters suggest values that should be merged.
questions.evidence: Clustering is a very powerful tool for cleaning datasets which contain misspelled or mistyped entries.

questions.q: Which file types can OpenRefine import?
options: Many, including TSV, CSV, Excel, JSON, XML and Google Spreadsheets
questions.explain: You create a project by importing data from your computer or the web.
questions.evidence: OpenRefine can import a variety of file types

questions.q: How does OpenRefine save your work?
options: It saves the project continuously, so you can close the browser and reopen it
questions.explain: Open Project on the start page continues where you left off.
questions.evidence: OpenRefine saves the project continuously so that you can close the browser

questions.q: What does OpenRefine's duplicates facet produce?
options: A true/false facet showing which values are duplicated
questions.explain: It's a quick way to find repeated records.
questions.evidence: this results in a binary facet of 'true' or 'false'

questions.q: What does OpenRefine's word facet do?
options: Breaks text into words and counts the records each word appears in
questions.explain: It helps spot inconsistent terms inside free-text columns.
questions.evidence: this breaks down text into words and counts the number of records each word appears in

questions.q: How can you return to the exact view of your facets and filters later?
questions.explain: The Permalink sits to the right of the project name.
questions.evidence: To save the exact view, you can bookmark the "Permalink"
